channel.title: Legacy Medical Blog
channel.description: Health notes from Legacy Medical, a Concierge Internal Medicine practice in Palm Beach Gardens, Florida.

item.title: Fiber: why it matters and how to get more
item.description: Fiber is linked to lower risk of heart disease, diabetes and colorectal cancer. How much to aim for, the two kinds, and simple ways to add it without discomfort.

item.title: Hydration for older adults: how much is enough
item.description: Thirst fades with age, and Florida heat raises the stakes. What the reference numbers say, the early signs of dehydration, and when drinking more is the wrong advice.

item.title: Women's health after 50: the checkups that matter
item.description: Mammograms, bone density, the heart, and when cervical screening can stop: the checkups national guidelines recommend for women over 50, with the year of each.

item.title: Men's health after 50: the checkups that matter
item.description: The screenings and vaccines that national guidelines recommend for men over 50, with the year each recommendation was issued, and the ones that call for a conversation first.

item.title: Mosquito-borne illness in Florida: dengue and West Nile basics
item.description: Palm Beach County has had a mosquito-borne illness advisory this year. What dengue and West Nile look like, who is at higher risk, and how to drain and cover.

item.title: Seasonal allergies in South Florida
item.description: Florida's pollen seasons run longer and overlap more than up north. What triggers allergies here, how to tell them from a cold, and which treatments work best.

item.title: Traveling with medications: packing, time zones and refills
item.description: How to pack prescriptions for a flight, handle doses across time zones and avoid running out when you split the year between two homes.

item.title: ER, urgent care or call your doctor: how to decide
item.description: When to call 911, when the emergency room is the right place, when urgent care will do, and when a call to your own doctor comes first. Stroke and heart attack signs included.

item.title: Reading your blood work: the CBC and metabolic panel in plain English
item.description: What each line on a complete blood count and a metabolic panel measures, and why a single flagged number is rarely the whole story.

item.title: How to prepare for a doctor's visit: a simple checklist
item.description: A short checklist for getting the most out of any appointment: what to write down, what to bring, and what to ask before you leave.

item.title: Advance directives in Florida: health care surrogate and living will basics
item.description: How Florida law handles a health care surrogate, a living will and decisions when there is no directive, with links to the statute. General information, not legal advice.

item.title: Caregiver burnout: looking after yourself while caring for a parent
item.description: Caring for a parent is meaningful and exhausting. The warning signs of caregiver stress, how to ask for help, and where to find respite.

item.title: Keeping your brain healthy: what the evidence supports
item.description: Blood pressure, hearing, exercise and social contact have real evidence behind them. Supplements and brain-training apps mostly do not. A plain look at the research.

item.title: Loneliness and social connection as a health issue
item.description: Loneliness and isolation are linked to heart disease, stroke, depression and dementia. What the research shows and practical ways to rebuild connection.

item.title: Depression in older adults: signs that are easy to miss
item.description: Depression in later life often looks like tiredness, aches or lost interest rather than sadness. The signs, what can mimic it, and how it is treated.

item.title: Eye health after 50: glaucoma, macular degeneration and cataracts
item.description: Three common eye conditions of later life, how each one shows up, who is at higher risk, and the eye symptoms that need same-day care.

item.title: Hepatitis C and hepatitis B screening for adults
item.description: The CDC now advises every adult to be tested for hepatitis C and hepatitis B at least once. Why, which blood tests are used, and what a positive result means today.

item.title: Abdominal aortic aneurysm screening: who should get the one-time ultrasound
item.description: A quick, painless ultrasound can find a weak spot in the body's largest artery before it causes trouble. Who the guidelines say should have it, and when.

item.title: Prostate cancer screening and the PSA test: making a shared decision
item.description: The PSA test is a choice, not a routine. What the official guidance says, the real numbers on benefit and harm, and questions to bring to your doctor.

item.title: Colon cancer screening: colonoscopy, stool tests and when to start
item.description: Screening for colorectal cancer now starts at 45. The test options, how often each one is repeated, and what happens after an abnormal result.
